questions.prompt: If the queen were ruling wisely, the citizens would not fear war.
questions.answer: Sī rēgīna sapienter regeret, cīvēs bellum nōn timērent.

questions.prompt: If you were braver, you would not flee the fierce enemy.
questions.answer: Sī fortior essēs, hostem ferōcem nōn fugerēs.

questions.prompt: If we had greater resources, we would build an immense wall.
questions.answer: Sī maiōrēs opēs habērēmus, mūrum inmēnsum exstruerēmus.

questions.prompt: If the poet were singing a sweeter song, the girl would listen gladly.
questions.answer: Sī poēta dulcius carmen caneret, puella libenter audīret.

questions.prompt: If the incautious soldier had watched the road, he would not have died.
questions.answer: Sī incautus mīles viam spectāvisset, nōn periisset.

questions.prompt: If you had torn away the chains, the captives would have fled.
questions.answer: Sī vincula revellissēs, captīvī fūgissent.

questions.prompt: If the general had trusted his allies, he would have conquered the fierce enemies.
questions.answer: Sī dux sociīs crēdidisset, ferōcēs hostēs vīcisset.

questions.prompt: If the mother had recognized the scar, she would have wept.
questions.answer: Sī māter cicātrīcem agnōvisset, flēvisset.

questions.prompt: If you come to Rome, you will see immense temples.
questions.answer: Sī Rōmam veniēs, templa inmēnsa vidēbis.

questions.prompt: If the enemies attack by night, we will defend the walls fiercely.
questions.answer: Sī hostēs nocte oppugnābunt, moenia ferōciter dēfendēmus.

questions.prompt: If you finish the task, I will give you a great reward.
questions.answer: Sī opus perfēceris, tibi magnum praemium dabō.

questions.prompt: Unless the storm ceases, the sailors will not set sail.
questions.answer: Nisi tempestās cessābit, nautae nōn nāvigābunt.

questions.prompt: If you are seeking wisdom, you read the poets carefully.
questions.answer: Sī sapientiam quaeris, poētās dīligenter legis.

questions.prompt: If the master is just, the servants love him.
questions.answer: Sī dominus iūstus est, servī eum amant.

questions.prompt: If innocence pleases the gods, the good are safe.
questions.answer: Sī innocentia deōs dēlectat, bonī tūtī sunt.

questions.prompt: If you are afraid, you conceal your wounds.
questions.answer: Sī timēs, vulnera tua cēlās.

questions.prompt: If I were king, I would free the innocent from prison.
questions.answer: Sī rēx essem, innocentēs ē carcere līberārem.

questions.prompt: If the lion had not mangled the shepherd, the flock would have been safe.
questions.answer: Sī leō pāstōrem nōn laniāvisset, grex tūtus fuisset.

questions.prompt: If you conquer fear, you will accomplish great deeds.
questions.answer: Sī metum vincēs, magna facinora efficiēs.

questions.prompt: If the general is wounded, the soldiers grieve.
questions.answer: Sī dux vulnerātus est, mīlitēs dolent.

questions.prompt: If the fields were fertile, the farmer would gather more crops.
questions.answer: Sī agrī fēcundī essent, agricola plūrēs frūgēs colligeret.

questions.prompt: If you had opened the gates, the enemies would have burst into the city.
questions.answer: Sī portās reclūsissēs, hostēs in urbem irrūpissent.

questions.prompt: If the winds are favorable, we will reach the shore within a month.
questions.answer: Sī ventī secundī erunt, ōram intrā mēnsem attingēmus.

questions.prompt: If you were telling the truth, I would trust you willingly.
questions.answer: Sī vēra dīcerēs, tibi libenter crēderem.

questions.prompt: If the general were braver, he would attack the enemy camp.
questions.answer: Sī dux fortior esset, castra hostium oppugnāret.

questions.prompt: If you were telling the truth, we would all believe you.
questions.answer: Sī vēra dīcerēs, tibi omnēs crēderēmus.

questions.prompt: If the dog were tame, the children would play in the garden.
questions.answer: Sī canis mānsuētus esset, līberī in hortō lūderent.

questions.prompt: If the poet were present, he would recite sublime verses.
questions.answer: Sī poēta praesēns esset, versūs sublīmēs recitāret.

questions.prompt: If the Helvetians had crossed the river, they would have destroyed the town.
questions.answer: Sī Helvētiī flūmen trānsīssent, oppidum dēlēvissent.

questions.prompt: If you had returned at evening, you would have found the gates closed.
questions.answer: Sī vespere revertissēs, portās clausās invēnissēs.

questions.prompt: If the magistrate had permitted it, the crowd would have entered the temple.
questions.answer: Sī magistrātus permīsisset, turba templum intrāvisset.

questions.prompt: If the baker had lit the oven, we would have eaten warm bread.
questions.answer: Sī pistor furnum incendisset, pānem calidum ēdissēmus.

questions.prompt: If you praise the brave, you encourage the young men.
questions.answer: Sī fortēs laudās, iuvenēs hortāris.

questions.prompt: If the soldiers are advancing slowly, the enemy is escaping.
questions.answer: Sī mīlitēs lentē prōcēdunt, hostis effugit.

questions.prompt: If the minister serves the king faithfully, he receives a reward.
questions.answer: Sī minister rēgī fidēliter servit, praemium accipit.

questions.prompt: If drums resound in the camp, the soldiers seize their arms.
questions.answer: Sī tympana in castrīs sonant, mīlitēs arma capiunt.

questions.prompt: If the Helvetians descend from the mountains, we will defend the bridge.
questions.answer: Sī Helvētiī dē montibus dēscendent, pontem dēfendēmus.

questions.prompt: If you return home at evening, you will hear the sublime song.
questions.answer: Sī vespere domum redībis, carmen sublīme audiēs.

questions.prompt: If the magistrate permits, we will build a new oven.
questions.answer: Sī magistrātus permittet, novum furnum aedificābimus.

questions.prompt: If mustard grows in the field, the farmer will sell it in the market.
questions.answer: Sī sināpis in agrō prōveniet, agricola eam in forō vēndet.

questions.prompt: Unless the citizens defend the walls, the city will be captured.
questions.answer: Nisi cīvēs mūrōs dēfendent, urbs capiētur.

questions.prompt: Unless the wound were serious, the doctor would not be worried.
questions.answer: Nisi vulnus grave esset, medicus nōn sollicitus esset.

questions.prompt: Unless the rowers had feared the storm, they would have set sail at first light.
questions.answer: Nisi rēmigēs tempestātem timuissent, prīmā lūce solvissent.

questions.prompt: Unless you obey the laws, you are harming the republic.
questions.answer: Nisi lēgibus pārēs, reī pūblicae nocēs.

questions.prompt: If the enemy had attacked by night, the guards would have fled in fear.
questions.answer: Sī hostēs noctū oppugnāvissent, custōdēs metū fūgissent.

questions.prompt: If the flame were spreading widely, the inhabitants would abandon their homes.
questions.answer: Sī flamma lātē diffunderētur, incolae domōs relinquerent.

questions.prompt: If the pupil does wrong, the teacher rebukes him.
questions.answer: Sī discipulus dēlinquit, magister eum reprehendit.

questions.prompt: If the last soldiers had reached the summit, they would have seen the victory.
questions.answer: Sī postrēmī mīlitēs summum montem attigissent, victōriam vīdissent.
